accepted.question_text: Let {gamma_k}_{k>=0} be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that f(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k/k! is an entire function. For parameters p with -p not in N, define the generalized Bessel-type function F_p(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k/(k! Gamma(k+p+1)). Characterize exactly which nonnegative sequences {gamma_k} make F_p belong to the Laguerre-Polya class of real entire functions.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Characterize all non-negative sequences {gamma_k}_0^infinity such that if f(x) = sum_{k=0}^infinity gamma_k x^k/k! is an entire function, then F_p(x) = sum_{k=0}^infinity gamma_k x^k/(k!Gamma(k + p + 1)) belongs to L - P, for -p notin N.

accepted.question_text: Does the sequence {ln(k+2)/k!}_{k>=0} form a multiplier sequence, meaning that the diagonal operator T[x^k]=(ln(k+2)/k!)x^k sends every real-rooted polynomial to another real-rooted polynomial?

evidence.quote: While we believe that the sequence {ln(k + 2)/k!}_0^infinity is a multiplier sequence, we were able to establish such a claim only for an approximating sequence.

accepted.question_text: Let {alpha_k}_{k>=0} and {beta_k}_{k>=0} be multiplier sequences of nonnegative real numbers. Characterize all functions Psi:R x R -> R such that the pointwise transformed sequence {Psi(alpha_k,beta_k)}_{k>=0} is again a multiplier sequence.

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Let {alpha_k}_0^infinity and {beta_k}_0^infinity be multiplier sequences of non-negative real numbers. Characterize all functions Psi : R x R -> R such that {Psi(alpha_k, beta_k)}_0^infinity is again a multiplier sequence.

accepted.question_text: Let p(x)=sum_{j=0}^n a_j x^j be a polynomial with a_j>=0. Find conditions on p(x) that make the sequence {p(k)/k!}_{k>=0} a multiplier sequence, and find conditions on p(x) that make {p(k)/k!}_{k>=0} a complex zero decreasing sequence, meaning that its diagonal operator does not increase the number of nonreal zeros of any real polynomial.

evidence.quote: Problem 36. Let p(x) := sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k, where a_k >= 0 (k >= 0). Find conditions on p(x) such that (a) {p(k)/k!}_0^infinity is a multiplier sequence and (b) {p(k)/k!}_0^infinity is a CZDS.

accepted.question_text: Is the sequence {(1+k+k^2)/k!}_{k>=0} a complex zero decreasing sequence, meaning that the diagonal operator T[x^k]=((1+k+k^2)/k!)x^k never increases the number of nonreal zeros of a real polynomial?

evidence.quote: Problem 37. Is the sequence {(1+k+k^2)/k!}_0^infinity a CZDS?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the sequence {sqrt(k)/k!}_{k>=0} is a multiplier sequence and whether it is a complex zero decreasing sequence. Equivalently for the first part, decide whether the entire function phi(x)=sum_{k>=0} sqrt(k) x^k/(k!k!) belongs to the Laguerre-Polya class with nonnegative coefficients.

evidence.quote: We conjecture that the function phi(x) = sum_{k=0}^infinity sqrt(k) x^k/(k!k!) belongs to L - P+.
Problem 39. Determine whether the sequence {sqrt(k)/k!} is (a) a multiplier sequence (b) a CZDS.

accepted.question_text: For each real s>0, does there exist an integer m>=1 such that the entire function sum_{k>=0} k^s x^k/(k!)^m belongs to L-P+, the Laguerre-Polya class of real entire functions with nonnegative Taylor coefficients?

evidence.quote: Problem 40. Is it true that for every s in R^+, there exists an m in N, such that sum_{k=0}^infinity k^s x^k/(k!)^m belongs to L - P+.

accepted.question_text: Let gamma_k=1/(k+1)^(k+1). Determine whether the sequence {gamma_k/k!}_{k>=0}={1/((k+1)^(k+1)k!)}_{k>=0} is a multiplier sequence, and determine whether it is a complex zero decreasing sequence.

evidence.quote: Problem 43. Let gamma_k := 1/(k + 1)^(k+1), k in N_0. Determine whether the sequence {gamma_k/k!}_0^infinity is (a) a multiplier sequence (b) a CZDS.

accepted.question_text: Characterize all multiplier sequences {gamma_k}_{k>=0} that admit a C_k-representation: there exist functions phi, Phi in L-P+ and real parameters s,t such that gamma_k = sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j) B_j^phi(t) B_{k-j}^Phi(s), where B_m^phi(u)=sum_{r=0}^m binom(m,r)(1-u)^r a_{m-r} u^{m-r} when phi(x)=sum_{m>=0} a_m x^m/m!.

evidence.quote: Definition 31. Let gamma_k in R for k = 0, 1, 2, .... We say that the sequence {gamma_k}_0^infinity has a C_k-representation, if there exist functions phi, Phi in L - P+ and s, t in R such that gamma_k = C_k^{phi,Phi}(t, s) for all k in N_0, where C_k^{phi,Phi}(t, s) is as defined in equation (4.2).
Problem 44. Characterize all multiplier sequences which have a C_k-representation.

accepted.question_text: Let beta_k=e^{sqrt(k)}/k!. The paper reports that the degree-n Jensen polynomials associated with {beta_k} have only real zeros for 1<=n<=30. Does that reality property continue for all degrees?

evidence.quote: On the other hand, our numerical work shows that the Jensen polynomials of degree n (1 <= n <= 30), associated with the sequence {beta_k}_0^infinity, have only real zeros.
